title: the DSG lodestone magnetism and the long-adventure NPC reactions

banner.title: The DSG LODESTONE AND NPC REACTIONS, R514: the printed pp. 42-43 (pdf 43-44) - the magnetic effects of lodestone (the iron-armor and iron-weapon effects, the innocuous iron-ore form that cannot impede movement or combat, the deep concentrated ores forming powerful magnetic rock, the Wisdom Check detection at 120 feet with the slight tug, the obvious-within-90-feet stage with the noticeable-but-not-pulling force, the threatened-within-30-feet stage with the strap-snapping pull on hanging iron, the Strength Checks for hand-held iron and iron armor with the 10-foot pull on a failed armor check, the no-repeat hold on a success, the checks repeated each 10 feet of approach, the -2 Strength at 20 feet and -4 at 10 feet, the -6 removal check with the forever-stuck failure, and the loss of all powers off-site) and the NPC reactions to long underground adventures (the special incentives, the Loyalty Check on being informed per DMG pages 36-37, the week-or-more trigger with the dwarf/gnome/drow exemption, the -5% per planned week, the -10% deception modifier, the -20%-month desert example, the separate roll per NPC, the avoidance short of risking life on a failure, the compelled NPC becoming unsteady, the slipping mind with the first-week ill effects, the 10% morale penalty and the nervous jumpiness, the weekly rechecks, the irrational break rolling d100 on Table 20, the four-band reactions grid, the effect lasting until slain or surfaced, and the 1d6 above-ground weeks with the recovery Wisdom Check and the permanent affliction on a failure)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 58-60 = the lodestone pages, idx 61-62 = the NPC pages) - every numeric cell dual-confirmed: the 120/90/30/10/10 distance ladder, the -2/-4/-6 penalties, the -5%/-10%/-20% Loyalty modifiers (the djvu garble -209/ settled by the Capture -20% read of the desert example) and the Table 20 bands confirmed by chapter djvu + the compiled-tables appendix reprint + Capture idx 62; the djvu garble ih place = in place settled by the appendix reprint. The Structural Decay section starts the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Table 20 pins as a 4x3 grid: the row key plus the lo and hi ends of each d100 band, with 00 read as 100 (the 86-00 band pins as 86-100). The percent and point penalties pin as positive magnitudes with the minus carried in the name and comment. The recovery period pins as dice + sides consts (1d6 weeks) per the R508 convention. The DMG pages 36-37 Loyalty seam and the Table 20 irrationality are noted; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnzWisCheckDetectionFt
consts.comment: the magnetic attraction of such rock can be detected by a character who passes a Wisdom Check when still 120 feet distant from the lodestone.

consts.name: dnzObviousWithinFt
consts.comment: the lodestone's effects become obvious to any characters moving within 90 feet.

consts.name: dnzThreatenedWithinFt
consts.comment: a character who comes within 30 feet of such a powerful lodestone becomes threatened.

consts.name: dnzArmorPullFt
consts.comment: a failed iron-armor Strength Check pulls the character 10 feet closer to the lodestone.

consts.name: dnzRepeatEveryFt
consts.comment: when the stone is approached, whether voluntarily or not, the Strength Checks must be repeated each 10 feet.

consts.name: dnzStrPenalty20Ft
consts.comment: a character suffers a -2 penalty to his Strength when 20 feet away (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzStrPenalty10Ft
consts.comment: a -4 penalty to Strength when only 10 feet away (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzRemovalStrPenalty
consts.comment: removing any iron object stuck to the lodestone requires a Strength Check with a -6 modifier (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzWeeklyLoyaltyPenaltyPct
consts.comment: a -5% modifier applies to the d100 Loyalty roll for every week that the party plans to spend underground (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzDeceptionPenaltyPct
consts.comment: an additional -10% modifier applies if the NPCs learn they have been deceived about the duration or destination of the expedition, or are told when it is too late for them to avoid it (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzExampleMonthPenaltyPct
consts.comment: the worked example: PCs leading henchmen across a blazing desert, then announcing a month underground, take a -20% Loyalty modifier for the month plus the -10% deception modifier (the djvu garble -209/, settled by the Capture -20% read; the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzMoralePenaltyPct
consts.comment: the unsteady character's morale is lowered by 10% for all Morale and Loyalty Checks (the magnitude of the penalty).

consts.name: dnzRecoveryWeeksDice
consts.comment: a character returned to the surface must spend 1d6 weeks above ground before a Wisdom Check is rolled for him - the dice count.

consts.name: dnzRecoveryWeeksSides
consts.comment: the above-ground recovery period die: d6.

consts.name: dnzT20RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 20 carries four reaction bands: running screaming to the surface, attacking a nearby PC, sneaking away quietly, and freezing in place.

bools.name: dnzMagnetismAffectsIronArmor
bools.comment: magnetism affects characters cloaked in iron armor, and can impede combat when iron weapons are used.

bools.name: dnzInnocuousFormInIronOre
bools.comment: lodestone in its more innocuous form is encountered frequently in areas containing iron ore.

bools.name: dnzInnocuousCannotImpede
bools.comment: in the common form the magnetic pull is barely strong enough to be noticed, and certainly cannot impede a character's movement or combat.

bools.name: dnzDeepOresPowerful
bools.comment: deep beneath the earth, concentrated ores of iron and other minerals have formed regions of massively powerful magnetic rock.

bools.name: dnzWisCheckSlightTug
bools.comment: the initial detection is manifested by nothing more than a slight tug on all iron possessions.

bools.name: dnzObviousNotPullingWill
bools.comment: within 90 feet the force upon metal objects is definitely noticeable, but still not capable of pulling a character against his will.

bools.name: dnzHangingIronSnapsStraps
bools.comment: when threatened, iron objects hanging on the character are pulled toward the lodestone with a force that can snap a thin leather strap.

bools.name: dnzStrCheckHandheldIron
bools.comment: the threatened character must make a Strength Check for all hand-held objects containing iron.

bools.name: dnzIronArmorExtraStrCheck
bools.comment: if the character is wearing iron armor, he must make an additional Strength Check.

bools.name: dnzSuccessHoldsNoRepeat
bools.comment: if the Strength Check is successful, the character retains hold of the item or holds his ground, and no further checks are required as long as he does not move closer to the stone.

bools.name: dnzRemovalFailForever
bools.comment: if the removal check fails, the character is forever unable to remove the object.

bools.name: dnzLosePowersOffSite
bools.comment: these lodestones lose all their powers if removed from their natural settings.

bools.name: dnzNpcsNeedSpecialIncentives
bools.comment: henchmen and hirelings lack the motivation of player characters for a prolonged underground expedition, and special incentives may be necessary to persuade the NPCs to remain underground.

bools.name: dnzLoyaltyCheckOnInformed
bools.comment: henchman and hireling loyalty should be checked as soon as they are informed of the nature of the expedition, with a normal Loyalty Check as explained on DMG pages 36 and 37.

bools.name: dnzCheckWeekOrMore
bools.comment: the Loyalty Check is required whenever a party plans to spend a week or more underground.

bools.name: dnzNoCheckDwarfGnomeDrow
bools.comment: the Loyalty Check is not necessary for dwarf, gnome, or drow NPCs.

bools.name: dnzSeparateRollPerNpc
bools.comment: each NPC, whether henchman or hireling, must be checked with a separate roll, and the DM should note all of the NPCs who fail the check.

bools.name: dnzFailureAvoidsMission
bools.comment: a failure on the Loyalty Check means the NPC does everything possible, short of risking his life, to avoid going on the mission.

bools.name: dnzCompelledBecomesUnsteady
bools.comment: an NPC compelled to accompany the party by circumstances or the PCs is considered to be unsteady.

bools.name: dnzUnsteadyMindSlips
bools.comment: an unsteady character becomes unsettled by long periods underground, away from sunlight and fresh air; his mind begins to slip, slowly at first, and finally in a fashion that can prove disastrous for himself and his companions.

bools.name: dnzIllEffectsAfterFirstWeek
bools.comment: the unsteady character begins to suffer ill effects following the first week underground.

bools.name: dnzNervousAndJumpy
bools.comment: the unsteady character acts nervous and jumpy.

bools.name: dnzLoyaltyCheckEachAddedWeek
bools.comment: following each additional week of underground exposure, another Loyalty Check is rolled for the character.

bools.name: dnzIrrationalOnFail
bools.comment: as soon as one of the weekly Loyalty Checks fails, the character becomes completely irrational, and the DM rolls 1d100 against Table 20: Unsteady NPC Reactions.

bools.name: dnzEffectUntilSlainOrSurface
bools.comment: effects determined on Table 20 last until the character is slain, or returned to the surface.

bools.name: dnzRecoveryWisCheck
bools.comment: if the recovery Wisdom Check succeeds, the character has recovered.

bools.name: dnzPermanentOnFail
bools.comment: if the recovery Wisdom Check fails, the character is permanently afflicted with the appropriate irrational behavior.

col_comments: the row key: 0 runs screaming toward the surface to the limits of his Endurance, 1 attacks a nearby PC, 2 attempts to sneak away quietly as soon as possible, 3 freezes in place, not reacting or moving.
